originality.rationale: The paper arxiv:2303.07880 (2023), Sections III--V, solves the linear two-slope ratchet and displays the finite-diffusivity entropy expression, with only a partial small-noise contribution (Section V, eq. 19). The present theorem applies to infinitely many non-piecewise-linear, variable-slope confining cusp potentials and proves that their limiting law and entropy constant depend only on the local cusp slopes. The 2024 full-text arxiv:2404.16955 reviews general entropy flux and names the ratchet as an external solved example but gives neither that universality theorem nor the exact cusp coefficient. arxiv:2008.08088 has hard reflecting walls and no periodic two-cusp drift. Searches of research results and historical claim inventories did not show an implication covering the variable-slope theorem. The finite-D linear formulas are acknowledged as prior knowledge; possible unindexed equivalent cusp results remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: The linear special case follows asymptotically from prior exact finite-D formulas, so its coefficient alone is not presented as a wholly independent new object.
The variable-slope universality may be equivalent to an unindexed singular perturbation theorem for active cusp diffusions.
A different entropy convention under time reversal need not obey this formula.

value.rationale: The limit resolves a physically motivated singular cancellation in stationary entropy production of an active ratchet. It shows that the coefficient and the entire local boundary layer are universal under nonlinear changes away from the attracting cusp, a structural extension beyond exactly solvable linear slopes. The coefficient can inform design of cusp confinement while revealing the distinct role of full-state entropy under vanishing thermal noise.
